title: $\cO_E$ is the profinite limit of its finite quotients $\cO_E/\pi_E^n$
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime and $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite extension, with its extending absolute value $|\cdot|_E$, ring of integers $\cO_E=\{x\in E:|x|_E\le1\}$, uniformizer $\pi_E$, finite quotient rings $A_n=\cO_E/\pi_E^n\cO_E$ $(n\ge1)$ and transition homomorphisms $A_{n+1}\to A_n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $q_n\colon\cO_E\to A_n$ be the reduction maps. Give $\cO_E$ the topology of $|\cdot|_E$, each $A_n$ the discrete topology, and $\varprojlim_nA_n=\{(b_n)\in\prod_{n\ge1}A_n: b_{n+1}\mapsto b_n\text{ for all }n\}$ the subspace topology of the product topology, with coordinatewise ring operations. Then:

1. The map $q=(q_n)_n\colon\cO_E\to\varprojlim_nA_n$ is an isomorphism of rings and a homeomorphism.
2. $\cO_E$ is a profinite space: compact, Hausdorff and totally disconnected.
3. For every finite set $Q$ with the discrete topology and every continuous surjection $g\colon\cO_E\to Q$ there is an $n\ge1$ such that $g$ factors as $g=h\circ q_n$ for a map $h\colon A_n\to Q$; such an $h$ is unique, and $g$ then factors uniquely through $q_m$ for every $m\ge n$.

source.place: Topology Tag 08ZU (theorem-tychonov) for compactness of the limit; Tag 0ET8 and Tag 08ZY (profinite spaces as limits of finite discrete spaces); for the local field input see literature/blueprint/main-20261015/blueprint/sec-proetale-coefficients/sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x/sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit.md, clause 1

proof.text:
Put $r=|\pi_E|_E$. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], $0<r<1$ and the units of $\mathcal O_E$ have absolute value $1$; by [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-absolute-value] the absolute value is nonarchimedean. For $z\in E$, division by $\pi_E^n$ gives
$$z\in\pi_E^n\mathcal O_E\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad |z|_E\le r^n.$$
Each coset $x+\pi_E^n\mathcal O_E$ is open: if $y$ belongs to it and $|z-y|_E<r^n$, the ultrametric inequality puts $z$ in it. Its complement is a union of the other cosets, so it is also closed. Since $r^n\to0$, these cosets, for $n\ge1$, form a neighbourhood basis at $x\in\mathcal O_E$. Finally [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients] supplies finiteness of $A_n$ and the surjective reduction transitions, with the stated ideals.

source.place: Clause 1: presentation of the profinite set of integers; explicit argument by Q139

proof.text: The reductions are compatible ring homomorphisms, so $q$ is a ring homomorphism to the displayed compatible-family ring $L=\varprojlim_n A_n$. If $q(x)=q(y)$, then step 1 gives $|x-y|_E\le r^n$ for every $n\ge1$. As $r^n\to0$, $|x-y|_E=0$, hence $x=y$. Thus $q$ is injective.

source.place: Clause 1: presentation of the profinite set of integers; explicit argument by Q139

proof.text: For $b=(b_n)\in L$, choose representatives $a_n\in\mathcal O_E$ of $b_n$. Compatibility implies $a_m-a_n\in\pi_E^n\mathcal O_E$ for every $m\ge n$, hence $|a_m-a_n|_E\le r^n$. Thus $(a_n)$ is Cauchy, and [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-complete] gives a limit $a\in E$. For each fixed $n$, choose $m\ge n$ sufficiently large that $|a-a_m|_E<r^n$. The ultrametric inequality gives $|a-a_n|_E\le r^n$. In particular $|a|_E\le\max(|a_n|_E,r^n)\le1$, so $a\in\mathcal O_E$, and $q_n(a)=b_n$ for every $n$. This proves surjectivity. A bijective ring homomorphism has a ring-homomorphic inverse: the inverse preserves each operation by applying $q$ and using injectivity. This proves the ring assertion of clause 1.

source.place: Clause 1: presentation of the profinite set of integers; explicit argument by Q139

proof.text: For $x\in\mathcal O_E$ let $C_n(q(x))=\{b\in L:b_n=q_n(x)\}$. These are open and closed coordinate cylinders, and $q^{-1}C_n(q(x))=x+\pi_E^n\mathcal O_E$. Moreover they form a neighbourhood basis in $L$: a product-basic neighbourhood restricts finitely many coordinates, and the cylinder at their maximum index is contained in it, by compatibility. Step 1 gives the corresponding basis on $\mathcal O_E$. Consequently $q$ and its inverse are continuous, proving the homeomorphism in clause 1.

source.place: Clause 1: presentation of the profinite set of integers; explicit argument by Q139

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-proper] to the given finite-dimensional extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extending absolute value. The closed ball $\{x\in E:|x|_E\le1\}$ is compact; it is exactly $\mathcal O_E$, with the topology prescribed in the statement. Thus $\mathcal O_E$ is compact.

source.place: Clause 1: presentation of the profinite set of integers; explicit argument by Q139

proof.text: The metric $d(x,y)=|x-y|_E$ makes $\mathcal O_E$ Hausdorff: distinct points have disjoint balls of radius $d(x,y)/3$. If a subset contains distinct $x,y$, step 2 provides an $n$ with $q_n(x)\ne q_n(y)$. The clopen coset $q_n^{-1}(q_n(x))$ and its complement separate that subset into two nonempty relatively open pieces. Thus every connected subset has at most one point. Together with step 5 this proves clause 2, with exactly the definition of profinite given in the item.

source.place: Tag 08ZY, lemma-profinite, forward implication: distinct points separated by a finite coordinate; metric separation written explicitly

proof.text: For the continuous $g:\mathcal O_E\to Q$, each fibre $g^{-1}(g(x))$ is open because $Q$ is discrete. By step 1 choose $n_x\ge1$ such that $U_x=x+\pi_E^{n_x}\mathcal O_E$ lies in that fibre. Compactness from step 5 gives a finite subcover $U_{x_1},\ldots,U_{x_t}$. It is nonempty since $0\in\mathcal O_E$. Put $n=\max_i n_{x_i}$. If $q_n(y)=q_n(z)$, select $i$ with $y\in U_{x_i}$. Then $z-y\in\pi_E^n\mathcal O_E\subseteq\pi_E^{n_{x_i}}\mathcal O_E$, hence $z\in U_{x_i}$ and $g(y)=g(z)$. Define $h(q_n(y))=g(y)$. This is well defined by the preceding calculation and is defined on all of $A_n$ since a quotient map is surjective. It satisfies $g=h\circ q_n$.

source.place: Tag 08ZZ, lemma-profinite-refine-open-covering, finite subcover followed by a common dominating index; specialized directly to the coset basis

proof.text: If $h'\circ q_n=g$, every $b\in A_n$ has a representative $y\in\mathcal O_E$, so $h'(b)=g(y)=h(b)$; hence $h'=h$. For $m\ge n$ let $\rho_{mn}:A_m\to A_n$ be reduction and put $h_m=h\circ\rho_{mn}$. Since $q_n=\rho_{mn}\circ q_m$, $h_m\circ q_m=g$. Surjectivity of $q_m$ gives uniqueness by the same representative calculation. This proves every assertion in clause 3; surjectivity of $g$ was not needed, so it certainly holds under the stated hypotheses.
